page.overview:
What is Dark Land?

The Dark Land, also referred to as the South Land or Southland, was a continent southeast of where the events of the and occurred. Little is known about its geographical features, but it may have several mountain ranges going through it, including the Yellow Mountains. The region called Southland in an earlier map was placed in the lower half of Arda, south of the Sea of Ringil between the Grey Mountains to the west and the Yellow Mountains to the east.

The Dark Land was created as a byproduct of the Battle of the Powers, in which the Valar overthrew Melkor in his original fortress of Utumno. Originally, Middle-earth was one landmass, set between the western sea of Belegaer and the Eastern Sea. This event split Middle-earth into two landmasses; the landmass to the south and east of the former Sea of Ringil (which was also called the "East Sea" by Tolkien) was known as the Dark Land.

No habitations in the Dark Land were ever recorded. The Númenóreans might have visited it on their long eastward journeys. If so, it is not known whether they established dwellings there.

In , Karen Wynn Fonstad depicted the continent in a map as being covered by vast forests bordering much of its shorelines.
